content.text: In this repo (Node 24, run TypeScript directly with `node scripts/generate_sample.ts`, no deps), create scripts/generate_sample.ts that generates SAMPLE (synthetic) electricity meter data for a fictional business "Crumb & Co" with three London bakery sites (S1 Shoreditch, S2 Brixton, S3 Hampstead). Window: 56 days, 2026-08-27T00:00:00Z to 2026-10-21T23:30:00Z inclusive, half-hourly UTC slots (2688 per site). Fetch REAL hourly temperature from https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=51.5072&longitude=-0.1276&start_date=2026-08-27&end_date=2026-10-21&hourly=temperature_2m&timezone=UTC (cache the response to data/cache/temp.json; reuse if present). Model kWh per half-hour per site = base load (fridges, lights, differs per site) + oven schedule (ovens on in early morning ~03:00-09:00 UTC weekdays, shorter Sundays, different per site) + heating sensitivity (extra kWh proportional to max(0, 15.5 - temp)) + small seeded noise (use a seeded PRNG, deterministic output). Plant these dated events into the data and record each in ops_log: S2 oven schedule moved 2h later from 2026-10-07 (new sourdough line); S3 one-off day 2026-09-20 with a freezer fault consuming extra kWh all day; S1 extra opening hours Saturdays from 2026-10-03. Write CSVs to data/sample/: meter_hh.csv (site_id,ts,kwh with ts like 2026-08-27T00:00:00Z, kwh 3 decimals), sites.csv (site_id,name,postcode,region,mpan_label), ops_log.csv (event_id,site_id,event_date,description), contract.csv (single row: product_code AGILE-24-10-01, tariff_code E-1R-AGILE-24-10-01-C, standing_charge_p_per_day 37.6525, vat_rate 0.05, valid_from 2026-08-27). Print a summary of total kWh per site. Every output should note it is sample data. Also add scripts/generate_sample.test.ts using node:test checking row counts (3*2688), determinism, no negative kWh. Run both and make sure they pass.
I'll explore the repo layout and any existing sample-data patterns, then implement the generator and tests.
